claim: As of July 2026 shadcn/ui defaults new projects to Base UI primitives; Radix remains supported but is no longer the default.
quote: New projects now default to Base UI. npx shadcn init defaults to Base UI as the default pick. The docs default to Base UI, with component pages opening on the Base UI tab. Radix is not being deprecated.

claim: MUI's official Tailwind v4 integration requires enableCssLayer, an explicit @layer order putting mui before utilities, and a hand-written @theme inline block mapping every --mui-* variable to a Tailwind theme variable.
quote: Set up the layer order so that `mui` comes before the `utilities` layer, allowing Tailwind CSS classes to override Material UI styles. @layer theme, base, mui, components, utilities; ... @theme inline { --color-primary: var(--mui-palette-primary-main); }

claim: Tailwind 4 theme variables declared with @theme both define a CSS custom property and generate utility classes; plain :root variables do not generate utilities; a theme can be shared across projects as an importable CSS file.
quote: Theme variables are special CSS variables defined using the @theme directive that influence which utility classes exist in your project. ... Use @theme when you want a design token to map directly to a utility class, and use :root for defining regular CSS variables that shouldn't have corresponding utilities.

claim: shadcn/ui theming is plain CSS custom properties in oklch under :root and .dark, exposed to Tailwind via @theme inline, with semantic background/foreground token pairs and a --radius base token.
quote: Define variables under :root and .dark selectors, expose to Tailwind via @theme inline directive, use resulting utility classes (e.g. bg-warning, text-warning-foreground). Dark Mode: Overrides same tokens within .dark selector.

claim: Base UI is unstyled and CSS-agnostic: className (string or state function), data-attributes for state, a style prop, and only layout-oriented CSS variables such as --available-height; it ships no theme object and no dark mode.
quote: Base UI components are unstyled and CSS-agnostic... Components expose state-specific data attributes (e.g., [data-checked])... Dynamic numeric values are exposed via CSS custom properties. For instance, Popover exposes --available-height and --anchor-width.

claim: Mantine generates --mantine-* CSS variables from its JS theme object, and cssVariablesResolver returns { variables, light, dark } to modify them or add custom variables.
quote: The cssVariablesResolver prop on MantineProvider accepts a function with this signature: (theme) => ({ variables: {...}, light: {...}, dark: {...} }). This enables modifying values of Mantine CSS variables or even adding your own variables.

claim: MUI's cssVariables mode supports colorSchemeSelector of media (default), class, data, or a custom pattern; cssVarPrefix renames or drops the --mui prefix; InitColorSchemeScript plus suppressHydrationWarning prevent the SSR flash for non-media selectors.
quote: Class-based: 'class' adds classes to the <html> element (.light, .dark). Data-attribute: 'data'. Custom selector: '.theme-%s'. The default uses media queries (@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)). ... Add InitColorSchemeScript for custom selectors (not media queries).

claim: Base UI 1.0 shipped 11 December 2025 with 35 accessible unstyled components and a package rename to @base-ui/react.
quote: The stable release occurred on December 11, 2025, featuring 35 unstyled UI components... The package name has changed from @base-ui-components/react to @base-ui/react.

claim: MUI has paused Pigment CSS to focus on Base UI, and Material UI v8 is still in the drafting stage as of 2026.
quote: drafting and shaping the feature set that will define the next major version of Material UI (v8)... Pigment CSS: Development remains paused... they decided to prioritize Base UI instead.

claim: A shadcn registry item can carry cssVars (theme/light/dark) and raw css rules, and the registry:theme and registry:style item types exist to distribute a design system.
quote: Registry items support a cssVars object with three sections: theme, light, dark. ... registry:style - Use for registry styles. registry:theme - Use for themes. Use css to add new rules to the project's CSS file eg. @layer base, @layer components, @utility, @keyframes, @plugin.

claim: Rhea (May 2026) is a denser shadcn style that adjusts component sizes and gaps directly rather than changing Tailwind's --spacing multiplier, so utilities like p-2 keep a stable meaning.
quote: a more compact Luma. Smaller spacing. Denser surfaces. Built for focused product interfaces... adjust component sizes, gaps, and density directly while keeping the underlying utility scale predictable.

claim: Mantine brand colors require 10-shade tuples (TypeScript error otherwise); generateColors/colorsTuple synthesise ramps, virtualColor maps one name onto different ramps per color scheme, and primaryShade can differ per scheme.
quote: A color tuple must contain at least 10 shades per color. Otherwise, you will get a TypeScript error... virtualColor({ name: 'primary', light: 'cyan', dark: 'pink' })... primaryShade: { light: 6, dark: 8 }

claim: Mantine's theme.variantColorResolver returns { background, hover, color, border } and centrally governs how every color-aware component renders each variant, including new custom variants.
quote: The theme.variantColorResolver must return an object with properties: background, hover, color, and border. It's a function to resolve colors based on variant... used to deeply customize how colors are applied to Button, ActionIcon, ThemeIcon and other components.

claim: MUI theme components expose defaultProps, slot-keyed styleOverrides with nested selectors, and a props-conditional variants array (now preferred over ownerState callbacks); custom variants and colors need TypeScript module augmentation.
quote: The variants key within styleOverrides enables conditional styling based on component props... Accessing slot ownerState through styleOverrides callbacks is no longer recommended... If you're using TypeScript, you'll need to specify new variants or colors using module augmentation.

claim: Tailwind 4's dark variant is class-based by default and must be redefined with @custom-variant to key off a data attribute.
quote: @custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *)) ... This approach is particularly useful for design systems that already use data attributes for theming instead of class-based approaches.

claim: Mantine sets data-mantine-color-scheme on <html> (via MantineProvider on the client, ColorSchemeScript pre-hydration on SSR) and persists the choice in the localStorage key mantine-color-scheme.
quote: sets a data-mantine-color-scheme attribute on the <html /> element... ColorSchemeScript... establishes the color scheme before hydration... By default, Mantine stores the color scheme value in localStorage using the key 'mantine-color-scheme'.

claim: Mantine documents the SSR flash-of-wrong-theme problem (FART) and states it can only occur in SSR/SSG apps, fixed by ColorSchemeScript.
quote: Flash of inaccurate color scheme (FART) happens when the color scheme selected by the user is different from the color scheme value with which the application has been initialized. FART can occur only in applications with server-side rendering (SSR) or static site generation (SSG).

claim: The DTCG Design Tokens Format Module uses JSON with $value/$type/$description, .tokens.json files and {group.token} aliases, but the June 2026 draft still carries a do-not-implement preview warning.
quote: This is a preview draft of in-progress changes... Do not attempt to implement this version of the specification. Do not reference this version as authoritative in any way. ... $value: Required property containing the token's data.

claim: Style Dictionary v4 has first-class DTCG support, using $value/$type/$description, and the DTCG and legacy formats cannot be mixed in one instance.
quote: As of version 4, Style Dictionary has first-class support for the DTCG format. The biggest difference is that the DTCG uses $value, $type and $description whereas the original format uses value, type and comment. In version 4 you can use either format, pick one though as they cannot be combined inside a single Style Dictionary instance.

claim: Style Dictionary ships both css/variables (CSS custom properties) and javascript/es6 / javascript/module / TypeScript declaration outputs, so tokens can be emitted as CSS or as a JS object.
quote: CSS Custom Properties are available via the css/variables format... JavaScript object outputs exist in multiple forms: javascript/module, javascript/module-flat, javascript/object, javascript/es6, javascript/esm.

claim: Merging multiple MUI themes requires manual deep-merging; passing multiple arguments to createTheme() is legacy behaviour that may be removed.
quote: only the first argument (options) is processed by the createTheme() function, and while passing multiple arguments currently works for backward compatibility, this behavior may be removed in future versions.

claim: MUI theme scoping (THEME_ID) exists chiefly to let Material UI coexist with a second Emotion/styled-components-based library, and MUI's own docs advise against running two styling libraries without a strong reason.
quote: Material UI can coexist with other component libraries that depend on Emotion or styled-components—this is possible thanks to theme scoping. ... Having more than one styling library can introduce unnecessary complexity to your project. You should have a very good reason to do this.

claim: Customising the palettes of MUI colorSchemes has open friction reported against the CSS-variables theme API.
quote: [material-ui] Unable to customize palettes of colorSchemes

claim: Mantine typed theme augmentation is a single mantine.d.ts file augmenting MantineThemeOther, MantineThemeColorsOverride (Record<CustomColors, MantineColorsTuple>) and MantineThemeSizesOverride.
quote: declare module '@mantine/core' { export interface MantineThemeColorsOverride { colors: Record<ExtendedCustomColors, MantineColorsTuple>; } }

claim: Under Tailwind 4, Mantine's default styles take precedence over Tailwind utilities unless the cascade layer order is fixed (theme, base, mantine, components, utilities) — a regression relative to Tailwind 3.
quote: in Tailwind v4, Mantine's default styles take precedence over Tailwind styles, unlike in v3 where Tailwind styles could be applied to Mantine components without problems... the recommended order is theme -> base -> mantine -> components -> utilities.
